RNC SEARCHING FOR WANTED MAN FOLLOWING DANGEROUS FLIGHT FROM POLICE
(Nov 19th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is searching for 22-year-old Joshua Roberts of Corner Brook, who is wanted on several charges following an incident Thursday morning.
Around 11:00 a.m. on November 19, the RNC received a report from a member of the public advising that Roberts was operating a vehicle believed to be stolen on Main Street in Corner Brook.
Operational Patrol Services responded and located the vehicle minutes later on Humber Road. Officers initiated a traffic safety stop, however, the driver, identified as Roberts, failed to stop and fled in a dangerous manner.
Police did not pursue the vehicle in the interest of public safety.
At approximately 11:30 a.m., the vehicle was located abandoned on West Street.
Roberts is wanted on charges of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle, possessing property obtained by crime, flight from police, and operating a vehicle while prohibited.
The RNC is actively seeking information to assist in locating Roberts, who is described as being 5’9” tall with blue eyes.
Anyone with information regarding his whereabouts is asked to contact the RNC at 709-637-4100.

RNCA WELCOMES BAIL REFORM FOLLOWING COURT DECISION
(Nov 19th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary Association (RNCA) is applauding a recent court decision to deny bail to an individual facing serious charges involving alleged intimate partner violence.
The association specifically recognized Justice Vikas Khaladkar for the decision, highlighting the importance of considering an individual’s history of violence, repeated breaches of court orders, and potential risks to victims and public safety when making bail decisions.
The RNCA is also welcoming the federal government’s new Bail and Sentencing Reform Act, which introduces stronger bail provisions for individuals charged with certain serious and repeat violent offences.
In a statement, the association said its members regularly witness the devastating impact of intimate partner violence and believes legislative changes that strengthen protections for victims and address the risks associated with repeat violent offenders are important steps toward safer communities.
The RNCA says it will continue advocating for a justice system that supports victims, protects the public, and provides the necessary tools to address repeat violent offending.

RNC SEIZES VEHICLE & DRUG PARAPHERNALIA
(Nov 19th)
A 26-year-old man is facing multiple charges following a traffic stop on Blackmarsh Road in St. John’s.
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) says Operational Patrol Services officers were conducting routine patrols around noon today when they observed a male, known to police to be prohibited from driving, operating a vehicle.
Officers conducted a traffic safety stop and arrested the driver.
During the arrest, officers observed items inside the vehicle believed to be indicative of drug trafficking. Both the driver and a female passenger were subsequently arrested for drug-related offences.
A search of the vehicle resulted in the seizure of four cell phones, prescription pills, cash, scales, knives and other drug paraphernalia.
The female passenger was released with charges pending, following the results of drug testing and further investigation by the RNC’s Weapons and Drugs Enforcement Unit.
The male driver has been charged with four counts of prohibited driving and one count of breach of probation. He also faces pending drug-related charges.
The vehicle was seized, and the man was held to appear in court.

WOMAN CHARGED WITH IMPAIRED DRIVING AFTER DEER LAKE CRASH
(Nov 19th)
A 65-year-old woman is facing impaired driving-related charges following a single-vehicle crash in Deer Lake on Tuesday night.
Shortly after 8:30 p.m. on November 17, police responded to a 911 call reporting a single vehicle off the road in the George Aaron Drive area.
The driver was located inside the vehicle and assessed by Emergency Medical Services personnel at the scene. No injuries were reported to police.
Officers noted signs of impairment by alcohol and issued a demand for a roadside breath test. The woman repeatedly failed to provide an adequate sample and was subsequently charged with failure or refusal to comply with a breath demand.
She is scheduled to appear in Provincial Court in January 2027 to answer to charges of failure or refusal to comply with a breath demand and impaired operation of a motor vehicle.
Her driver’s licence was suspended, and the vehicle was towed from the scene and impounded.

SHED FIRE QUICKLY KNOCKED DOWN BY SJRFD FIREFIGHTERS
(Nov 19th)
Firefighters with the St. John’s Regional Fire Department (SJRFD) responded to a reported structure fire at a residential property on Pearson Street Thursday morning (November 19th).
Just before 8:40 a.m., crews were called to the property located between Lorne Place and Lansdowne Place.
Upon arrival, firefighters located smoke coming from a shed at the rear of the property. Crews quickly deployed an attack line and made quick work of the fire.
An SJRFD Platoon Chief confirmed to NFLD Bulletin at the scene that a nearby neighbour noticed smoke coming from the shed and called 911.
The Platoon Chief also confirmed that nobody was home at the time of the fire and there were no injuries reported.
The shed sustained moderate to extensive damage to its interior.

RNC CELEBRATES 40 YEARS OF POLICING IN CORNER BROOK
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is celebrating 40 years of policing in the city of Corner Brook, marking four decades of service and commitment to public safety in the region.
On July 1, 1986, then-Chief E. Donald Randell addressed the first shift as the RNC returned to Corner Brook for the first time since 1950, expanding its policing operations from the Northeast Avalon and Labrador West.
Since returning to the city, the RNC says it has worked to establish a policing standard the community can rely on, crediting the continued support of the communities it serves, along with the dedication and pride of its members.
In 2024, the RNC’s jurisdiction expanded to include communities along the Bay of Islands, the Town of Massey Drive, and communities throughout the Humber Valley, including Pasadena.
Retirees, current officers, civilian staff, and community members gathered at the RNC’s Corner Brook detachment today to mark the milestone.
The RNC recognized the contributions of officers past and present, highlighting their continued commitment to public safety over the past four decades and thanking them for their service.
As the force celebrates the anniversary, it says it looks ahead with confidence and purpose, committed to building on its legacy of service and helping create safer, stronger communities for generations to come.

TWO DRIVERS FACE IMPAIRED DRIVING CHARGES IN METRO REGION
(Nov 19th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) conducted two impaired driving investigations following separate traffic stops in St. John’s on Tuesday evening.
At approximately 9:36 p.m. on November 18, 2026, members of Operational Patrol Services conducted a traffic stop on Waldergrave Street. After detecting the smell of alcohol on the driver, officers began an impaired driving investigation.
The male driver registered a warn on an approved roadside screening device. Police seized and impounded the vehicle and issued the driver a seven-day licence suspension.
Just 14 minutes later, at approximately 9:50 p.m., officers conducted another traffic stop in the area of St. Thomas Line.
Police quickly observed that the 48-year-old male driver was significantly impaired by alcohol. He was transported to the RNC’s Mount Pearl office, where he failed both breathalyzer samples.
When officers attempted to release the accused, he tore up his release papers and indicated that he intended to continue driving, stating that he had several vehicles and would not attend court.
Police seized the accused’s driver’s licence, impounded his vehicle and transported him to the city lockup.
The 48-year-old was charged with impaired operation of a motor vehicle and operating a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding 80 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood.

WANTED MAN - ANDREW PARSONS
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is seeking the public’s assistance in locating wanted person Andrew Parsons of St. John’s.
Operational Patrol Services responded to a St. John’s residence for a report of an assault by the complainant’s former partner on Nov. 11.
The RNC’s Criminal Investigation Division was engaged and as a result of an investigation, Andrew Parsons, 51, is wanted and believed to be actively evading police.
Parsons, originally from Nova Scotia, is wanted on charges of assault, two counts of uttering threats, forcible confinement, assault causing bodily harm, and five counts of violence against an intimate partner.
Parsons is described to be 5’10” tall and 180 lbs with dark, greying hair. (See photo attached).
The RNC is asking anyone with information on his whereabouts to contact 709-729-8000.

MISSING TEENAGER - BURIN PENINSULA
(Nov 18th)
~ 10:30 p.m; Burin Peninsula RCMP is asking for the public’s help to locate 16-year-old Kendra Clarke. Police and family are concerned for her well-being and would like to speak with her as soon as possible.
Clarke was last seen around 9:00 p.m. on Wednesday (November 18). Police believe she may be in the Janes Pond area of Marystown.
She is approximately 5’ 8” (172cm) tall and 210 lbs (95 kg), with dark red or burgundy hair and blue eyes. She was last seen wearing a black jacket and dark coloured (black or dark grey) pants.
If you have information about the current location or recent movements of Kendra Clarke, please contact the Burin Peninsula RCMP detachment at 709-279-3001 or call 1-800-709-RCMP (7267).

DRIVER CAUGHT TRAVELLING 115 KM/H ON TORBAY ROAD
(Nov 18th)
A driver had her licence suspended and vehicle impounded after being caught travelling more than double the posted speed limit on Torbay Road in St. John’s Wednesday morning.
At approximately 10:30 a.m., a member of Traffic Services observed a vehicle travelling at 115 km/h in a posted 50 km/h zone.
As a result, the female driver was ticketed, her licence was suspended, and the vehicle was impounded.

MAN CHARGED WITH SEXUAL ASSAULT ON FLIGHT TO ST. JOHN’S
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) has charged a 33-year-old Burin man with sexual assault following an incident aboard a flight destined for St. John’s.
The RNC received a report around 10 p.m. on Monday, November 17, regarding a sexual assault involving two passengers who were not known to one another.
Operational Patrol Services officers removed the male suspect from the plane and arrested him for sexual assault. He was held for court.
The RNC is encouraging all survivors of sexual violence to reach out to a trusted resource for support as soon as it is safe to do so.
Members of the RNC’s Child Abuse and Sexual Assault Unit are available to speak with anyone who has information or questions. Officers take a trauma-informed approach, providing education about legal and investigative options while directing survivors to appropriate resources based on their individual circumstances and needs.
The RNC can be reached at 709-729-8000. Anyone requiring immediate assistance is urged to call 911.

RNC URGES ONLINE SHOPPERS TO BE CAUTIOUS THIS HOLIDAY SEASON
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is reminding online shoppers to exercise caution this holiday season, warning that fraudsters are looking to take advantage of shoppers through fake websites, misleading deals and phishing messages.
As people shop for the perfect gifts to put under the tree, scammers are creating fraudulent websites, advertising too-good-to-be-true deals, and sending convincing emails and text messages designed to steal personal and financial information.
The RNC is encouraging shoppers to take steps to protect their information and avoid falling victim to online fraud.
Police recommend buying only from trusted websites and verifying a retailer's authenticity. Shoppers are encouraged to type a retailer's web address directly into their browser rather than clicking on links.
Offers that appear too good to be true should also raise suspicion. Aggressive discounts, poorly designed websites and a lack of contact information may be warning signs of a fraudulent website.
The RNC also recommends making purchases using personal devices and secure networks rather than public Wi-Fi, keeping devices updated and maintaining active antivirus protection.
Shoppers are encouraged to protect their accounts by using strong, unique passwords and enabling multi-factor authentication where available.
The RNC further advises shoppers to monitor bank and credit card statements for unfamiliar charges, track deliveries and avoid leaving shipments unattended.
Anyone who suspects they have been a victim of fraudulent activity is encouraged to report it to the RNC at 709-729-8000 or the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at 1-800-495-8501.

ALERT READY TEST TO TAKE PLACE THIS MORNING

THREE ARRESTED FOLLOWING BREAK-AND-ENTER AT FORMER WATERFORD HOSPITAL
(Nov 17th)
Three 18-year-old males have been arrested and charged following a break-and-enter at the former Waterford Hospital in St. John’s early Sunday morning, November 15th.
Shortly after midnight, officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary’s (RNC) Operational Patrol Services and Police Dog Services were called to the scene.
When NFLD Bulletin arrived, officers had surrounded the former Administrative Building on the property.
In a response to NFLD Bulletin on Tuesday, November 17th, the RNC confirmed that three 18-year-old males were arrested at the scene.
All three were released to appear in court at a later date, each facing a single charge of break and enter.

MARYSTOWN JUNIOR FIREFIGHTER PROGRAM CELEBRATES 10TH ANNIVERSARY
(Nov 17th)
The Marystown Junior Firefighter Program is celebrating its 10th anniversary, marking a decade of providing young people with an opportunity to learn about firefighting and gain experience alongside members of the Fire Department.
Over the past 10 years, a total of 78 students have enrolled in the program, with several returning to take on additional responsibilities and some going on to serve in the fire service.
Of those students, 19 returned for a second year as Assistant Instructors, also known as Peer Leaders, while six returned for a third year in the same role.
Three former participants later returned to serve with the Marystown Fire Department, including Jayden, who is currently serving with the department as the program’s Committee Chairperson. Two other participants are serving or have served with neighbouring fire departments.
The 2026 Junior Firefighter Class recently wrapped up its 10-week program, with participants taking part in their final training session on the department’s training grounds before gathering for a banquet at the Fire Hall.
The final training session provided an opportunity for the students to put their learning into practice, with the department thanking its firefighters for providing instruction and oversight throughout the program.
The department extended its appreciation to the Town of Marystown, its firefighters, and the official sponsors who helped make the program possible, including Tina Belliveau (Co-operators), Coady’s Git er done LTD, Burin Peninsula Voice Against Violence, and Hickman Chevrolet Buick GMC Burin.
Additional thanks were extended to Adam’s Candy Sparkes for providing sweet treats, as well as Brushett’s Auto, Newco Metal & Auto Recycling Ltd. in Marystown, and Subway for their in-kind support and donations throughout the program.
With the 10th anniversary now celebrated, the department congratulated the 2026 Junior Firefighter Class and all former participants who have taken part over the years.
The program will welcome another group of students in 2027, with applications expected to open in late February.
/Info: Marystown Volunteer Fire Department.
